completeCard.name: Arcane Bolt
completeCard.effect: Arcane Bolt. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, universal, damage. Make a Wizard spell attack. On a hit deal S d6 + M force damage. Arcane Bolt is an always-prepared class matrix once acquired and uses the normal first-distinct-matrix and Refrain rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Bolt: Launch a bolt of pure arcane energy that deals force damage to a single target.

completeCard.name: Arcane Shield
completeCard.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
completeCard.effect: Arcane Shield. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, abjuration, protection. Trigger when an attack roll would hit you. Gain +2 AC against the triggering attack and until the start of your next regular turn, potentially causing the attack to miss. Temporary AC from another Arcane Shield does not stack.

source.originalText: Arcane Shield: Create a barrier of magical force that provides temporary protection.

completeCard.name: Arcane Insight
completeCard.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. When examining an active magical effect, spell residue, magic item or arcane construction, you may make an Intelligence (Arcana) check to determine its broad school, function or unusual matrix behavior. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no invented fact.

source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-wizards.

completeCard.name: Spell Scribing
completeCard.effect: Spell Scribing. Tags: base, passive, spellbook. Copying a legal found Wizard spell into your spellbook requires 1 hour and 25 gp of inks and components per spell rank, treating rank 0 as rank 1 for this calculation, instead of the pilot baseline 2 hours and 50 gp. Level-up spells remain free.

source.originalText: Spell Scribing: Copy spells into your spellbook at half the normal cost and time.

completeCard.name: Spellbook Study
completeCard.effect: Spellbook Study. Tags: base, active, matrix, ritual. Replace one currently prepared matrix with one legal spell recorded in your spellbook. The replacement must be within your Wizard rank limit. This is the normal midday substitution permission; it does not alter the spellbook, create another prepared-matrix position or reset first-cast/Refrain history for an underlying matrix family already cast this encounter.

source.originalText: Spellbook Study: Spend time studying your spellbook to prepare a different selection of spells.

completeCard.name: Scholarly Mind
completeCard.effect: Scholarly Mind. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. You have advantage on Intelligence checks whose primary purpose is recalling, researching or analyzing arcane theory, magical history, planar magical principles or constructed spell formulae. It does not grant advantage on spell attacks, Counterspell checks or general Investigation unrelated to arcane scholarship.

source.originalText: Scholarly Mind: Gain advantage on Intelligence checks related to arcane knowledge.

completeCard.name: Arcane Sight
completeCard.effect: Arcane Sight. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, divination, concentration. While active you perceive magical auras within 60 feet and automatically know each visible aura's school or broad magical category. As an Action on a later turn, examine one aura to learn whether it is concentrated, summoned, cursed, warded or linked to another visible magical effect. Total cover blocks sight.

source.originalText: Arcane Sight: See magical auras and effects for a short duration.

completeCard.name: Sigil Rewrite
completeCard.effect: Sigil Rewrite. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, matrix. Replace one prepared matrix with a different spell from your spellbook of exactly the same rank without performing the normal 10-minute ritual. The replacement receives no special Dissonance reset for a matrix family already used this encounter and must obey current Wizard rank eligibility.

source.originalText: Sigil Rewrite: Once/day, instantly swap a spell you know for another of the same tier

completeCard.name: Matrix Efficiency
completeCard.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. This does not reduce the separate 10-minute midday substitution ritual, spell scribing, rituals or spellbook reconstruction unless another feature explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

completeCard.name: Matrix Mastery
completeCard.effect: Matrix Mastery. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. During preparation you may assign at most one common Matrix Mastery modification to each ordinary prepared spell: Quick Substitution, Component Enhancement, Matrix Linking or Stability Reinforcement, using the exact common definitions in the Wizard engine. Always-prepared class-card matrices cannot receive these modifications unless a card explicitly says otherwise.

source.originalText: Matrix Mastery: Modify spell matrices to change minor aspects of prepared spells.

completeCard.name: Floating Preparation
completeCard.effect: Floating Preparation. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. Increase your maximum prepared Spell Matrix count by 1. The extra matrix can come from any school and obeys all ordinary spellbook and rank restrictions. It is a prepared matrix for every rule, including protected strain, duplicate-family tracking and Matrix Mastery modifications.

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

completeCard.name: Spell Tether
completeCard.effect: Spell Tether. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, concentration, tether. When you begin a second concentration spell that targets only yourself while already concentrating on a self-only spell, spend 3 additional RP. For up to 3 rounds you may maintain both. Whenever damage requires a concentration save, make one save; failure ends BOTH spells. Starting a third concentration effect ends both tethered spells before the new one begins. Spell Tether and Tethered Cast cannot be combined; maximum two sustained concentration effects total. Only one Spell Tether can exist at a time.

source.originalText: Spell Tether: Maintain 2 self-buff spells without concentration (1/rest)

completeCard.name: Improved Concentration
completeCard.effect: Improved Concentration. Tags: arch, passive, concentration. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made because damage threatens your concentration on a Wizard spell. This does not alter the DC, protect a Tether from rules that explicitly end both effects, or prevent Silence, incapacitation and other non-damage concentration failures.

source.originalText: Improved Concentration: Advantage on concentration checks when taking damage.

completeCard.name: Dispel Magic
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet
completeCard.effect: Dispel Magic. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Choose one ongoing spell effect you can perceive. If its rank is 3 or lower, end it. If it is rank 4 or higher, make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + spell rank; success ends it. Permanent artifact properties and effects explicitly immune to dispelling are unaffected.

source.originalText: Dispel Magic: End magical effects in an area or on a target.

completeCard.name: Spell Preservation
completeCard.effect: Spell Preservation. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, spellbook. Your primary spellbook cannot be destroyed, erased or rendered permanently unreadable by non-artifact mundane or magical means. It can still be stolen, hidden, transported, suppressed, sealed by an artifact-level effect or voluntarily abandoned. Copies and backup books do not automatically receive this protection.

source.originalText: Spell Preservation: Your spellbook cannot be destroyed by non-artifact means.

completeCard.name: Seal Magic
completeCard.effect: Seal Magic. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, control. Choose one of the eight schools and target one creature. It makes a Wisdom save. On failure it cannot cast spells of the chosen school. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending the Seal on success. The effect ends automatically after 3 rounds and never prevents non-spell class techniques merely because they are magical.

source.originalText: Seal Magic: Prevent a target from casting spells of a specific school (WIS save, 3 rounds)

completeCard.name: Arcane Lock
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One door, chest, portal or unattended object within touch
completeCard.effect: Arcane Lock. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Magically seal the target. Opening it without your permission requires a Strength check or thieves'/arcane-tool check against your Wizard spell DC. Dispel Magic can end the lock. You can designate up to M creatures who can bypass it. This does not make the object physically indestructible.

source.originalText: Arcane Lock: Create a magical barrier that prevents entry or access to an object or area.

completeCard.name: Knowledge Shield
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: Allies directly protected by one of your Abjuration Wizard spells
completeCard.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
completeCard.frequency: At most once per ally per round
completeCard.effect: Knowledge Shield. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, protection. When you cast an Abjuration spell that grants AC, temporary HP, resistance or a saving-throw benefit to an ally, that ally also gains +2 on its next saving throw before the start of your next regular turn. Multiple Knowledge Shields do not stack.

source.originalText: Knowledge Shield: When you cast a protective spell, allies gain +2 to saving throws.

completeCard.name: Dimensional Pocket
completeCard.effect: Dimensional Pocket. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, conjuration, ritual. Create an extradimensional storage space holding up to 100 pounds or 10 cubic feet of unattended nonliving material. Retrieving or placing an item while adjacent to the opening uses an object interaction. Living creatures cannot enter. When duration ends, remaining contents appear harmlessly in the nearest unoccupied space.

source.originalText: Dimensional Pocket: Create a small extradimensional space to store items.

automaticCards.name: Arcane Tradition
automaticCards.frequency: Automatic at Wizard 3; not a selection
automaticCards.effect: Arcane Tradition. Tags: arch, school, automatic. Your level-1 Arcane School becomes your Arcanist tradition; do not choose a second school. Prepare one additional matrix from that same school each day without counting it against your normal prepared-matrix maximum. It otherwise obeys all ordinary rank, spellbook, Dissonance and duplicate-family rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Tradition: Choose a school of magic to specialize in, gaining bonuses to spells of that school.

automaticCards.name: Counterspell
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One creature you perceive casting a spell within 60 feet
automaticCards.effect: Counterspell. Tags: arch-source, automatic, wizard-spell, abjuration, disruption. Trigger when a creature begins casting a spell. Make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + twice the spell's rank, treating rank 0 as 0. Success negates the triggering spell after its costs are paid; failure lets it resolve. This is gained automatically at Wizard 2 and is never also selected from the Arch pool.

source.originalText: Counterspell: Disrupt an enemy's spellcasting, potentially negating their spell entirely.

automaticCards.name: Elemental Affinity
automaticCards.duration: Permanent until changed by Core Sync
automaticCards.frequency: Automatic when Elementalist is chosen; counts as one level-10 Hero acquisition
automaticCards.effect: Elemental Affinity. Tags: hero, elementalist, elemental, automatic. Choose Fire, Cold, Lightning or Earth when entering Elementalist. Fire corresponds to fire damage, Cold to cold, Lightning to lightning and Earth to magical bludgeoning damage created by earth effects. Wizard spells matching the affinity gain +2 to their Wizard save DC or +2 on their spell attack, as applicable, and once per spell add one extra die matching that spell's primary damage die to one damage roll.

source.originalText: Elemental Affinity: Choose 1 element (Fire, Ice, Lightning, Earth); all spells of that element gain +2 DC, +1 damage tier

automaticCards.name: Ritual Casting
automaticCards.cost: 0 RP unless the individual ritual explicitly states otherwise
automaticCards.frequency: At will outside encounters with sufficient time
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5184. Cast a Wizard spell bearing the Ritual tag directly from your spellbook without preparing it. Increase its casting time by at least 10 minutes. Ritual Casting cannot be completed during an encounter, does not use an ordinary prepared-matrix position and does not generate or vent normal casting Dissonance.

source.originalText: | 2 | Counterspell Reaction, Ritual Casting |

automaticCards.name: School Mastery
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5186. This is the one School Mastery progression grant, not a second school choice or duplicate feat. Increase the level-1 Arcane School spell-attack and spell-save bonus from +1 to +2 total. Its school passive and bonus-spell rules otherwise remain unchanged.

source.originalText: | 5 | Bonus Feat: School Mastery |

automaticCards.name: Arcane Ward
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5187. After preparing spells, choose one of acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, psychic, radiant or thunder that is dealt by at least one prepared spell of your Arcane School. Gain resistance to that damage type until your next long rest. If none of your prepared school spells deals a damage type, choose force. This is provisional completion of the source's ambiguous 'chosen school's element' wording.

source.originalText: | 6 | Arcane Ward (resistance to chosen school's element) |

automaticCards.name: Dual Cast
automaticCards.cost: Pay the complete RP costs of both spells
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5188. Choose two DIFFERENT prepared Wizard spells of rank 1 or 2, neither of which summons a creature or grants an additional Action. Cast both sequentially as one Action, paying both RP costs. They cannot both require concentration. Each matrix separately updates first-cast/Refrain history. Features that trigger merely from 'casting a spell' may trigger once for each actual matrix unless that feature itself says once per turn; no trigger may create another Dual Cast or additional full Action.

source.originalText: | 9 | Dual Cast (cast 2 Tier 1–2 spells in a round) |

automaticCards.name: Overchannel
automaticCards.cost: Pay the Core V 2 RP cost for one rank above the spell's normal cast rank
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One prepared spell you are beginning to cast
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5190. Cast one prepared spell as though it were one rank higher than the highest rank at which you could normally cast that SAME spell, provided the spell has an explicit higher-rank scaling rule. Overchannel does not teach or prepare a higher-rank spell, cannot exceed effective rank 9 and cannot be combined with another generic Overcast rule during this pilot. All normal Dissonance/Refrain rules still apply.

source.originalText: | 13 | Overchannel (cast a spell 1 tier higher once/day) |

completeCard.name: Arcane Shield
completeCard.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
completeCard.effect: Arcane Shield. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, abjuration, protection. Trigger when an attack roll would hit you. source.originalText: Arcane Shield: Create a barrier of magical force that provides temporary protection.

completeCard.name: Arcane Insight
completeCard.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. When examining an active magical effect, spell residue, magic item or arcane construction, you may make an Intelligence (Arcana) check to determine its broad school, function or unusual matrix behavior. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no invented fact.

source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-wizards.

completeCard.name: Spell Scribing
completeCard.effect: Spell Scribing. Tags: base, passive, spellbook. Copying a legal found Wizard spell into your spellbook requires 1 hour and 25 gp of inks and components per spell rank, treating rank 0 as rank 1 for this calculation, instead of the pilot baseline 2 hours and 50 gp. Level-up spells remain free.

source.originalText: Spell Scribing: Copy spells into your spellbook at half the normal cost and time.

completeCard.name: Spellbook Study
completeCard.effect: Spellbook Study. Tags: base, active, matrix, ritual. Replace one currently prepared matrix with one legal spell recorded in your spellbook. The replacement must be within your Wizard rank limit. This is the normal midday substitution permission; it does not alter the spellbook, create another prepared-matrix position or reset first-cast/Refrain history for an underlying matrix family already cast this encounter.

source.originalText: Spellbook Study: Spend time studying your spellbook to prepare a different selection of spells.

completeCard.name: Scholarly Mind
completeCard.effect: Scholarly Mind. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. You have advantage on Intelligence checks whose primary purpose is recalling, researching or analyzing arcane theory, magical history, planar magical principles or constructed spell formulae. It does not grant advantage on spell attacks, Counterspell checks or general Investigation unrelated to arcane scholarship.

source.originalText: Scholarly Mind: Gain advantage on Intelligence checks related to arcane knowledge.

completeCard.name: Arcane Sight
completeCard.effect: Arcane Sight. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, divination, concentration. While active you perceive magical auras within 60 feet and automatically know each visible aura's school or broad magical category. As an Action on a later turn, examine one aura to learn whether it is concentrated, summoned, cursed, warded or linked to another visible magical effect. Total cover blocks sight.

source.originalText: Arcane Sight: See magical auras and effects for a short duration.

completeCard.name: Sigil Rewrite
completeCard.effect: Sigil Rewrite. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, matrix. Replace one prepared matrix with a different spell from your spellbook of exactly the same rank without performing the normal 10-minute ritual. The replacement receives no special Dissonance reset for a matrix family already used this encounter and must obey current Wizard rank eligibility.

source.originalText: Sigil Rewrite: Once/day, instantly swap a spell you know for another of the same tier

completeCard.name: Matrix Efficiency
completeCard.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. This does not reduce the separate 10-minute midday substitution ritual, spell scribing, rituals or spellbook reconstruction unless another feature explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

completeCard.name: Matrix Mastery
completeCard.effect: Matrix Mastery. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. During preparation you may assign at most one common Matrix Mastery modification to each ordinary prepared spell: Quick Substitution, Component Enhancement, Matrix Linking or Stability Reinforcement, using the exact common definitions in the Wizard engine. Always-prepared class-card matrices cannot receive these modifications unless a card explicitly says otherwise.

source.originalText: Matrix Mastery: Modify spell matrices to change minor aspects of prepared spells.

completeCard.name: Floating Preparation
completeCard.effect: Floating Preparation. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. Increase your maximum prepared Spell Matrix count by 1. The extra matrix can come from any school and obeys all ordinary spellbook and rank restrictions. It is a prepared matrix for every rule, including protected strain, duplicate-family tracking and Matrix Mastery modifications.

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

completeCard.name: Spell Tether
completeCard.effect: Spell Tether. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, concentration, tether. When you begin a second concentration spell that targets only yourself while already concentrating on a self-only spell, spend 3 additional RP. For up to 3 rounds you may maintain both. Whenever damage requires a concentration save, make one save; failure ends BOTH spells. Starting a third concentration effect ends both tethered spells before the new one begins. Spell Tether and Tethered Cast cannot be combined; maximum two sustained concentration effects total. Only one Spell Tether can exist at a time.

source.originalText: Spell Tether: Maintain 2 self-buff spells without concentration (1/rest)

completeCard.name: Improved Concentration
completeCard.effect: Improved Concentration. Tags: arch, passive, concentration. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made because damage threatens your concentration on a Wizard spell. This does not alter the DC, protect a Tether from rules that explicitly end both effects, or prevent Silence, incapacitation and other non-damage concentration failures.

source.originalText: Improved Concentration: Advantage on concentration checks when taking damage.

completeCard.name: Dispel Magic
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet
completeCard.effect: Dispel Magic. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Choose one ongoing spell effect you can perceive. If its rank is 3 or lower, end it. If it is rank 4 or higher, make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + spell rank; success ends it. Permanent artifact properties and effects explicitly immune to dispelling are unaffected.

source.originalText: Dispel Magic: End magical effects in an area or on a target.

completeCard.name: Spell Preservation
completeCard.effect: Spell Preservation. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, spellbook. Your primary spellbook cannot be destroyed, erased or rendered permanently unreadable by non-artifact mundane or magical means. It can still be stolen, hidden, transported, suppressed, sealed by an artifact-level effect or voluntarily abandoned. Copies and backup books do not automatically receive this protection.

source.originalText: Spell Preservation: Your spellbook cannot be destroyed by non-artifact means.

completeCard.name: Seal Magic
completeCard.effect: Seal Magic. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, control. Choose one of the eight schools and target one creature. It makes a Wisdom save. On failure it cannot cast spells of the chosen school. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending the Seal on success. The effect ends automatically after 3 rounds and never prevents non-spell class techniques merely because they are magical.

source.originalText: Seal Magic: Prevent a target from casting spells of a specific school (WIS save, 3 rounds)

completeCard.name: Arcane Lock
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One door, chest, portal or unattended object within touch
completeCard.effect: Arcane Lock. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Magically seal the target. You can designate up to M creatures who can bypass it. This does not make the object physically indestructible.

source.originalText: Arcane Lock: Create a magical barrier that prevents entry or access to an object or area.

source.originalText:
Spellcasting
Drawing on the essence of nature itself, you can cast spells to shape that essence to your will. See chapter 10 for the general rules of spellcasting and chapter 11 for the druid spell list.
Cantrips
At 1st level, you know two cantrips of your choice from the druid spell list. You learn additional druid cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Druid table.
Preparing and Casting Spells
The Druid table shows how many Resonance Points you have to cast your druid spells. A spell's base RP cost is twice its Resonance Rank (Rank 0 cantrips cost 0), modified by explicit class features and current Dissonance. You regain expended RP according to the Resonance recovery rules.
You prepare the list of druid spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the druid spell list. When you do so, choose a number of druid spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your druid level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have Resonance Points.
For example, if you are a 3rd-level druid, you have 7 Resonance Points. With a Wisdom of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells, and they can be of 1st or 2nd level in any combination. If you prepare the Rank 1 spell cure wounds, its base cost is 2 Resonance Points before explicit specialization or Dissonance modifiers. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.
You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of druid spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.
Spellcasting Ability
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your druid spells, since your magic draws upon your devotion and attunement to nature. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a druid spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Ritual Casting
You can cast a druid spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

Spellcasting Focus
You can use a druidic focus as a spellcasting focus for your druid spells.

source.originalText:
Shapeshifting
At 1st level, you gain the ability to transform into various animal forms. Shapeshifting is Aethel's native druidic transformation discipline and functions according to the following rules:

Activation and Duration
You can use a bonus action to assume a beast form. You can remain in beast form for 10 minutes per use. You then revert to your normal form unless you expend another use of this feature. You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn.

Uses per Day
At 1st level, you can use your Shapeshifting ability twice per long rest. You gain additional uses as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Shapeshifting Uses column of the Druid table.

Available Forms
At 1st level, you can transform into any of the Base Druid Forms listed below. At 11th level, you gain access to Arch Druid Forms. At 10th level, you gain access to Hero Druid Forms specific to your chosen Circle.
Limitations While Transformed
While in beast form:
You cannot cast spells unless specified by your Hero Class
Your ability to speak is limited (only preserved in arch/hero forms)
You retain your mental ability scores (Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma)
You gain the physical traits of the chosen form as specified

source.originalText:
Spellcasting
Drawing on the essence of nature itself, you can cast spells to shape that essence to your will. See chapter 10 for the general rules of spellcasting and chapter 11 for the druid spell list.
Cantrips
At 1st level, you know two cantrips of your choice from the druid spell list. You learn additional druid cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Druid table.
Preparing and Casting Spells
The Druid table shows how many Resonance Points you have to cast your druid spells. A spell's base RP cost is twice its Resonance Rank (Rank 0 cantrips cost 0), modified by explicit class features and current Dissonance. You regain expended RP according to the Resonance recovery rules.
You prepare the list of druid spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the druid spell list. When you do so, choose a number of druid spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your druid level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have Resonance Points.
For example, if you are a 3rd-level druid, you have 7 Resonance Points. With a Wisdom of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells, and they can be of 1st or 2nd level in any combination. If you prepare the Rank 1 spell cure wounds, its base cost is 2 Resonance Points before explicit specialization or Dissonance modifiers. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.
You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of druid spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.
Spellcasting Ability
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your druid spells, since your magic draws upon your devotion and attunement to nature. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a druid spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Ritual Casting
You can cast a druid spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

Spellcasting Focus
You can use a druidic focus as a spellcasting focus for your druid spells.

At 1st level, you gain the ability to transform into various animal forms. Shapeshifting is Aethel's native druidic transformation discipline and functions according to the following rules:

You can use a bonus action to assume a beast form. You can remain in beast form for 10 minutes per use. You then revert to your normal form unless you expend another use of this feature. You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn.

Uses per Day
At 1st level, you can use your Shapeshifting ability twice per long rest. You gain additional uses as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Shapeshifting Uses column of the Druid table.

Available Forms
At 1st level, you can transform into any of the Base Druid Forms listed below. At 11th level, you gain access to Arch Druid Forms. At 10th level, you gain access to Hero Druid Forms specific to your chosen Circle.
Limitations While Transformed
While in beast form:
You cannot cast spells unless specified by your Hero Class
Your ability to speak is limited (only preserved in arch/hero forms)
You retain your mental ability scores (Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma)
You gain the physical traits of the chosen form as specified

completeEngine: Charisma governs Oath DC/M and divine technique attacks. Weapon attacks use their ordinary Strength/Dexterity ability. Hit Die d10; all armor, shields, simple and martial weapons. Paladin has no Conviction or Oracle Revelation Charges. Lay on Hands is its own pool, 5×Paladin level, fully restored only by long rest. Ordinary spells and printed Smite fuel use the same Paladin Core V 2 RP pool; healing points never convert to RP.

Base progression is explicit rather than the ordinary 25-card template: at 1 automatically gain Lay on Hands, Divine Sense, Martial Proficiency, Divine Strike, Protective Stance and Sacred Touch. At 2 gain Righteous Challenge, Bolstering Presence, Fighting Style and ordinary Paladin spell access. At 3 swear ONE of ten Oaths; gain only its Smite modification, Aura and first Revelation spell. This Oath is the Arch specialization. At 10 enter Hero Oath Mastery of that SAME Oath; no second Oath or additional generic Hero tree. Signature Power unlocks 11, Final Gift 20. Oath Revelations automatically unlock 3/5/9/13/17, always known in addition to the shared spell repertoire, rank 1/2/3/4/5 respectively. Exact printed RP costs replace generic cost only if the card explicitly supplies them.

At 2 choose one Fighting Style: Defense +1 AC while armored; Dueling +2 damage to first one-handed melee hit on your own turn; Protection Reaction impose disadvantage on one attack against an adjacent ally when using a shield. At 3 Divine Health gives advantage on disease saves, not universal immunity. At 5 Extra Attack makes two attacks when taking the ordinary Attack Action; named attack techniques use their own counts. These three features reconcile preserved main-registry entries; other old level-table extras, including extra level 14 ASI and undefined free slot riders, are not stacked into this draft. ASI/feat at 4/8/12/16/19 follows general advancement once.

Divine Strike at 1: after one melee weapon hit on your regular turn, spend 1 RP to add S d6 radiant. At 2 this becomes Divine Smite: choose 1 RP for S d6 or 2 RP for(S+1)d8 radiant, once/own turn total. Oath 3 changes type/rider as its card states, never adds another copy of the base damage. Smite is not an ordinary spell, cannot be counterspelled or generically Overcast, and causes no Dissonance. A critical hit doubles Smite damage dice under ordinary rules, but never healing, resources or percentage copies.

One Oath aura, requires consciousness and no concentration. Radius 10 ft at 3, 15 ft at 6, 20 ft at 10, 30 ft at 15. Benefits affect up to 3 allies or 3 enemies as the Oath card states, chosen at start of your turn and changed next turn; they must stay within aura. At 6 choose one additional aura benefit for that day: allies+1 saves against fear/charm, or 1 flat DR against weapon damage. At 7 once/short rest when enemy damages an ally in aura, Reaction make one melee attack if in reach; may pay normal Smite cost even off turn, but total Smite maximum one per round from this reactive feature. At 10 aura persists until start of your next regular turn after incapacitation; then ends if still incapacitated. At 15 also grant selected allies+1 initiative while in aura when initiative is rolled; no retroactive turn changes.

At 17 Aura Surge once/short rest Bonus Action: until start next turn choose up to 3 allies in aura to gain S+M temporary HP and+1 saves. This bounded surge replaces vague doubling of every aura number. At 20 Divine Manifestation makes the aura active upon initiative without an action, radius 30 ft; it ignores ordinary Silence and terrain obstruction between allies but not antimagic explicitly suppressing divine powers, planar barriers or the consciousness rule. Source cannot-be-suppressed language is bounded explicitly. It grants no free Signature, Smite or Revelation spell.

Protected interface: Smite, Aura and Lay on Hands generate no Weave Dissonance. After a successful direct melee hit, your next Oath spell before end next turn generates 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0, consuming the benefit. No stacking, RP discount or Refrain reset. Oath Revelation spells and the five replacement Forbidden spells below are ordinary spells for strain, countering and concentration; signature powers and final gifts are Oath techniques unless expressly tagged otherwise.

Oath conduct clauses remain intact in source and Oath cards. The Director identifies a relevant clause and a knowingly chosen serious breach before applying a fall. A disagreement, failed roll, coerced act or unknown fact does not silently remove a character. A fall is an explicit story transition recorded with the player: choose the corresponding Oathbreaker inversion or pursue an agreed restoration scene. Preserve class level and already spent resources. Oathbreaker replaces its Oath Aura, Smite rider, Signature and Revelation list, rather than stacking both sets. Base martial abilities remain; Lay on Hands becomes Death Touch using the same current 5 L pool, with no refill on switching.

Death Touch baseline: Action melee divine attack PB+CHA; declare and spend 1 through 2 S+M points before the attack from remaining Lay on Hands pool to deal that much necrotic damage (choose amount before roll; miss still spends declared points). Each Oath inversion may alter type or add its bounded rider; never copy innate traits, confiscate class engines or automatically execute a target. A listed inverted Signature is available only at 11 and replaces the ordinary Signature use, one/short rest. An inverted aura follows the same radius, target cap and timing. Oathbreaker 20 uses the new Black Manifestation common capstone instead of its original Final Gift.

The source names a Forbidden Spell List but does not supply five complete entries for each inversion. This pilot explicitly adds one shared five-spell replacement list (below), with each Oathbreaker using its inversion name as flavor. These are new test rules, not recovered historical spells. Choose the normal Oath package OR inverted package at a time. All later Oath prerequisites still use Paladin class level; the Oathbreaker label does not bypass 3/11/20 gates.

Oath integration limits: one paid Smite total per round, including the level-7 Reaction; one Oath-aura reactive event per round. Multiple damage-redirection options share one event per round unless Crown Undying expressly allows two. Apply original-target defenses once, then split actual damage; transferred damage cannot be mitigated again, reflected, redirected again or generate resources. This explicit rule supersedes wording that permits recipient defenses again.

Sustained Oath spell damage/healing zones use concentration, at most three pulses, and 1 RP upkeep after the first pulse unless a priced card expressly supplies a different finite cadence. Native Oath auras retain their printed passive cadence and target cap. Final auras last their stated finite duration and include their pulses. All hard-denial effects, including compelled Actions, share the common once/source/target/encounter guard; later failures only remove Reactions and reduce Speed by half for one turn.

An emergency Reaction whose trigger itself incapacitates you, such as Grace Reversal or Thorn Crown, may resolve before that incapacitation only if you had a Reaction available before the triggering event. This grants no other actions while incapacitated. Narrative labels such as oppressor require a specific act of captivity/coercion established in the scene, not an alignment or identity assumption.

The source ceiling’s half-pool-per-round Lay on Hands cap is a preserved alternative. This pilot instead uses maximum class level per ordinary Lay on Hands Action and the explicitly once-per-long-rest level-17 Wave that distributes the current remaining pool. No normal heal gains the Wave’s exception.

For any one damage event choose exactly one Paladin redirection feature. Using it consumes the shared redirection allowance for that round. Crown Undying permits two DIFFERENT ally-damage events per round, but still only one redirection feature may modify each event.

PR11.heroPath: Oath Mastery Oathbreaker — Oath of Chains Broken
completeEngine: Charisma governs Oath DC/M and divine technique attacks. Weapon attacks use their ordinary Strength/Dexterity ability. Hit Die d10; all armor, shields, simple and martial weapons. Paladin has no Conviction or Oracle Revelation Charges. Lay on Hands is its own pool, 5×Paladin level, fully restored only by long rest. Ordinary spells and printed Smite fuel use the same Paladin Core V 2 RP pool; healing points never convert to RP.

Base progression is explicit rather than the ordinary 25-card template: at 1 automatically gain Lay on Hands, Divine Sense, Martial Proficiency, Divine Strike, Protective Stance and Sacred Touch. At 2 gain Righteous Challenge, Bolstering Presence, Fighting Style and ordinary Paladin spell access. At 3 swear ONE of ten Oaths; gain only its Smite modification, Aura and first Revelation spell. This Oath is the Arch specialization. At 10 enter Hero Oath Mastery of that SAME Oath; no second Oath or additional generic Hero tree. Signature Power unlocks 11, Final Gift 20. Oath Revelations automatically unlock 3/5/9/13/17, always known in addition to the shared spell repertoire, rank 1/2/3/4/5 respectively. Exact printed RP costs replace generic cost only if the card explicitly supplies them.

At 2 choose one Fighting Style: Defense +1 AC while armored; Dueling +2 damage to first one-handed melee hit on your own turn; Protection Reaction impose disadvantage on one attack against an adjacent ally when using a shield. At 3 Divine Health gives advantage on disease saves, not universal immunity. At 5 Extra Attack makes two attacks when taking the ordinary Attack Action; named attack techniques use their own counts. These three features reconcile preserved main-registry entries; other old level-table extras, including extra level 14 ASI and undefined free slot riders, are not stacked into this draft. ASI/feat at 4/8/12/16/19 follows general advancement once.

Divine Strike at 1: after one melee weapon hit on your regular turn, spend 1 RP to add S d6 radiant. At 2 this becomes Divine Smite: choose 1 RP for S d6 or 2 RP for(S+1)d8 radiant, once/own turn total. Oath 3 changes type/rider as its card states, never adds another copy of the base damage. Smite is not an ordinary spell, cannot be counterspelled or generically Overcast, and causes no Dissonance. A critical hit doubles Smite damage dice under ordinary rules, but never healing, resources or percentage copies.

One Oath aura, requires consciousness and no concentration. Radius 10 ft at 3, 15 ft at 6, 20 ft at 10, 30 ft at 15. Benefits affect up to 3 allies or 3 enemies as the Oath card states, chosen at start of your turn and changed next turn; they must stay within aura. At 6 choose one additional aura benefit for that day: allies+1 saves against fear/charm, or 1 flat DR against weapon damage. At 7 once/short rest when enemy damages an ally in aura, Reaction make one melee attack if in reach; may pay normal Smite cost even off turn, but total Smite maximum one per round from this reactive feature. At 10 aura persists until start of your next regular turn after incapacitation; then ends if still incapacitated. At 15 also grant selected allies+1 initiative while in aura when initiative is rolled; no retroactive turn changes.

At 17 Aura Surge once/short rest Bonus Action: until start next turn choose up to 3 allies in aura to gain S+M temporary HP and+1 saves. This bounded surge replaces vague doubling of every aura number. At 20 Divine Manifestation makes the aura active upon initiative without an action, radius 30 ft; it ignores ordinary Silence and terrain obstruction between allies but not antimagic explicitly suppressing divine powers, planar barriers or the consciousness rule. Source cannot-be-suppressed language is bounded explicitly. It grants no free Signature, Smite or Revelation spell.

Protected interface: Smite, Aura and Lay on Hands generate no Weave Dissonance. After a successful direct melee hit, your next Oath spell before end next turn generates 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0, consuming the benefit. No stacking, RP discount or Refrain reset. Oath Revelation spells and the five replacement Forbidden spells below are ordinary spells for strain, countering and concentration; signature powers and final gifts are Oath techniques unless expressly tagged otherwise.

Oath conduct clauses remain intact in source and Oath cards. The Director identifies a relevant clause and a knowingly chosen serious breach before applying a fall. A disagreement, failed roll, coerced act or unknown fact does not silently remove a character. A fall is an explicit story transition recorded with the player: choose the corresponding Oathbreaker inversion or pursue an agreed restoration scene. Preserve class level and already spent resources. Oathbreaker replaces its Oath Aura, Smite rider, Signature and Revelation list, rather than stacking both sets. Base martial abilities remain; Lay on Hands becomes Death Touch using the same current 5 L pool, with no refill on switching.

Death Touch baseline: Action melee divine attack PB+CHA; declare and spend 1 through 2 S+M points before the attack from remaining Lay on Hands pool to deal that much necrotic damage (choose amount before roll; miss still spends declared points). Each Oath inversion may alter type or add its bounded rider; never copy innate traits, confiscate class engines or automatically execute a target. A listed inverted Signature is available only at 11 and replaces the ordinary Signature use, one/short rest. An inverted aura follows the same radius, target cap and timing. Oathbreaker 20 uses the new Black Manifestation common capstone instead of its original Final Gift.

The source names a Forbidden Spell List but does not supply five complete entries for each inversion. This pilot explicitly adds one shared five-spell replacement list (below), with each Oathbreaker using its inversion name as flavor. These are new test rules, not recovered historical spells. Choose the normal Oath package OR inverted package at a time. All later Oath prerequisites still use Paladin class level; the Oathbreaker label does not bypass 3/11/20 gates.

Oath integration limits: one paid Smite total per round, including the level-7 Reaction; one Oath-aura reactive event per round. Multiple damage-redirection options share one event per round unless Crown Undying expressly allows two. Apply original-target defenses once, then split actual damage; transferred damage cannot be mitigated again, reflected, redirected again or generate resources. This explicit rule supersedes wording that permits recipient defenses again.

Sustained Oath spell damage/healing zones use concentration, at most three pulses, and 1 RP upkeep after the first pulse unless a priced card expressly supplies a different finite cadence. Native Oath auras retain their printed passive cadence and target cap. Final auras last their stated finite duration and include their pulses. All hard-denial effects, including compelled Actions, share the common once/source/target/encounter guard; later failures only remove Reactions and reduce Speed by half for one turn.

An emergency Reaction whose trigger itself incapacitates you, such as Grace Reversal or Thorn Crown, may resolve before that incapacitation only if you had a Reaction available before the triggering event. This grants no other actions while incapacitated. Narrative labels such as oppressor require a specific act of captivity/coercion established in the scene, not an alignment or identity assumption.

The source ceiling’s half-pool-per-round Lay on Hands cap is a preserved alternative. This pilot instead uses maximum class level per ordinary Lay on Hands Action and the explicitly once-per-long-rest level-17 Wave that distributes the current remaining pool. No normal heal gains the Wave’s exception.

For any one damage event choose exactly one Paladin redirection feature. Using it consumes the shared redirection allowance for that round. Crown Undying permits two DIFFERENT ally-damage events per round, but still only one redirection feature may modify each event.

completeCard.name: Matrix Efficiency
completeCard.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

completeCard.name: Matrix Mastery

source.originalText: Matrix Mastery: Modify spell matrices to change minor aspects of prepared spells.

completeCard.name: Floating Preparation

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

completeCard.name: Spell Tether
completeCard.effect: Spell Tether. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, concentration, tether. source.originalText: Spell Tether: Maintain 2 self-buff spells without concentration (1/rest)

completeCard.name: Improved Concentration
completeCard.effect: Improved Concentration. Tags: arch, passive, concentration. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made because damage threatens your concentration on a Wizard spell. source.originalText: Improved Concentration: Advantage on concentration checks when taking damage.

completeCard.name: Dispel Magic
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet

completeCard.name: Arcane Bolt
completeCard.effect: Arcane Bolt. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, universal, damage. Make a Wizard spell attack. On a hit deal S d6 + M force damage. Arcane Bolt is an always-prepared class matrix once acquired and uses the normal first-distinct-matrix and Refrain rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Bolt: Launch a bolt of pure arcane energy that deals force damage to a single target.

completeCard.name: Arcane Shield
completeCard.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
completeCard.effect: Arcane Shield. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, abjuration, protection. Trigger when an attack roll would hit you. Gain +2 AC against the triggering attack and until the start of your next regular turn, potentially causing the attack to miss. Temporary AC from another Arcane Shield does not stack.

source.originalText: Arcane Shield: Create a barrier of magical force that provides temporary protection.

completeCard.name: Arcane Insight
completeCard.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. When examining an active magical effect, spell residue, magic item or arcane construction, you may make an Intelligence (Arcana) check to determine its broad school, function or unusual matrix behavior. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no invented fact.

source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-wizards.

completeCard.name: Spell Scribing
completeCard.effect: Spell Scribing. Tags: base, passive, spellbook. Copying a legal found Wizard spell into your spellbook requires 1 hour and 25 gp of inks and components per spell rank, treating rank 0 as rank 1 for this calculation, instead of the pilot baseline 2 hours and 50 gp. Level-up spells remain free.

source.originalText: Spell Scribing: Copy spells into your spellbook at half the normal cost and time.

completeCard.name: Spellbook Study
completeCard.effect: Spellbook Study. Tags: base, active, matrix, ritual. Replace one currently prepared matrix with one legal spell recorded in your spellbook. The replacement must be within your Wizard rank limit. This is the normal midday substitution permission; it does not alter the spellbook, create another prepared-matrix position or reset first-cast/Refrain history for an underlying matrix family already cast this encounter.

source.originalText: Spellbook Study: Spend time studying your spellbook to prepare a different selection of spells.

completeCard.name: Scholarly Mind
completeCard.effect: Scholarly Mind. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. You have advantage on Intelligence checks whose primary purpose is recalling, researching or analyzing arcane theory, magical history, planar magical principles or constructed spell formulae. It does not grant advantage on spell attacks, Counterspell checks or general Investigation unrelated to arcane scholarship.

source.originalText: Scholarly Mind: Gain advantage on Intelligence checks related to arcane knowledge.

completeCard.name: Arcane Sight
completeCard.effect: Arcane Sight. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, divination, concentration. While active you perceive magical auras within 60 feet and automatically know each visible aura's school or broad magical category. As an Action on a later turn, examine one aura to learn whether it is concentrated, summoned, cursed, warded or linked to another visible magical effect. Total cover blocks sight.

source.originalText: Arcane Sight: See magical auras and effects for a short duration.

completeCard.name: Sigil Rewrite
completeCard.effect: Sigil Rewrite. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, matrix. Replace one prepared matrix with a different spell from your spellbook of exactly the same rank without performing the normal 10-minute ritual. The replacement receives no special Dissonance reset for a matrix family already used this encounter and must obey current Wizard rank eligibility.

source.originalText: Sigil Rewrite: Once/day, instantly swap a spell you know for another of the same tier

completeCard.name: Matrix Efficiency
completeCard.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. This does not reduce the separate 10-minute midday substitution ritual, spell scribing, rituals or spellbook reconstruction unless another feature explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

completeCard.name: Matrix Mastery
completeCard.effect: Matrix Mastery. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. During preparation you may assign at most one common Matrix Mastery modification to each ordinary prepared spell: Quick Substitution, Component Enhancement, Matrix Linking or Stability Reinforcement, using the exact common definitions in the Wizard engine. Always-prepared class-card matrices cannot receive these modifications unless a card explicitly says otherwise.

source.originalText: Matrix Mastery: Modify spell matrices to change minor aspects of prepared spells.

completeCard.name: Floating Preparation
completeCard.effect: Floating Preparation. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. Increase your maximum prepared Spell Matrix count by 1. The extra matrix can come from any school and obeys all ordinary spellbook and rank restrictions. It is a prepared matrix for every rule, including protected strain, duplicate-family tracking and Matrix Mastery modifications.

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

completeCard.name: Spell Tether
completeCard.effect: Spell Tether. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, concentration, tether. When you begin a second concentration spell that targets only yourself while already concentrating on a self-only spell, spend 3 additional RP. For up to 3 rounds you may maintain both. Whenever damage requires a concentration save, make one save; failure ends BOTH spells. Starting a third concentration effect ends both tethered spells before the new one begins. Spell Tether and Tethered Cast cannot be combined; maximum two sustained concentration effects total. Only one Spell Tether can exist at a time.

source.originalText: Spell Tether: Maintain 2 self-buff spells without concentration (1/rest)

completeCard.name: Improved Concentration
completeCard.effect: Improved Concentration. Tags: arch, passive, concentration. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made because damage threatens your concentration on a Wizard spell. This does not alter the DC, protect a Tether from rules that explicitly end both effects, or prevent Silence, incapacitation and other non-damage concentration failures.

source.originalText: Improved Concentration: Advantage on concentration checks when taking damage.

completeCard.name: Dispel Magic
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet
completeCard.effect: Dispel Magic. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Choose one ongoing spell effect you can perceive. If its rank is 3 or lower, end it. If it is rank 4 or higher, make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + spell rank; success ends it. Permanent artifact properties and effects explicitly immune to dispelling are unaffected.

source.originalText: Dispel Magic: End magical effects in an area or on a target.

completeCard.name: Spell Preservation
completeCard.effect: Spell Preservation. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, spellbook. Your primary spellbook cannot be destroyed, erased or rendered permanently unreadable by non-artifact mundane or magical means. It can still be stolen, hidden, transported, suppressed, sealed by an artifact-level effect or voluntarily abandoned. Copies and backup books do not automatically receive this protection.

source.originalText: Spell Preservation: Your spellbook cannot be destroyed by non-artifact means.

completeCard.name: Seal Magic
completeCard.effect: Seal Magic. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, control. Choose one of the eight schools and target one creature. It makes a Wisdom save. On failure it cannot cast spells of the chosen school. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending the Seal on success. The effect ends automatically after 3 rounds and never prevents non-spell class techniques merely because they are magical.

source.originalText: Seal Magic: Prevent a target from casting spells of a specific school (WIS save, 3 rounds)

completeCard.name: Arcane Lock
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One door, chest, portal or unattended object within touch
completeCard.effect: Arcane Lock. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Magically seal the target. Opening it without your permission requires a Strength check or thieves'/arcane-tool check against your Wizard spell DC. Dispel Magic can end the lock. You can designate up to M creatures who can bypass it. This does not make the object physically indestructible.

source.originalText: Arcane Lock: Create a magical barrier that prevents entry or access to an object or area.

completeCard.name: Knowledge Shield
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: Allies directly protected by one of your Abjuration Wizard spells
completeCard.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
completeCard.frequency: At most once per ally per round
completeCard.effect: Knowledge Shield. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, protection. When you cast an Abjuration spell that grants AC, temporary HP, resistance or a saving-throw benefit to an ally, that ally also gains +2 on its next saving throw before the start of your next regular turn. Multiple Knowledge Shields do not stack.

source.originalText: Knowledge Shield: When you cast a protective spell, allies gain +2 to saving throws.

completeCard.name: Dimensional Pocket
completeCard.effect: Dimensional Pocket. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, conjuration, ritual. Create an extradimensional storage space holding up to 100 pounds or 10 cubic feet of unattended nonliving material. Retrieving or placing an item while adjacent to the opening uses an object interaction. Living creatures cannot enter. When duration ends, remaining contents appear harmlessly in the nearest unoccupied space.

source.originalText: Dimensional Pocket: Create a small extradimensional space to store items.

completeCard.name: Spell Absorption
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One hostile spell that directly targets you
completeCard.effect: Spell Absorption. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, abjuration. Trigger after you become the target of a hostile spell but before it resolves. Make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + twice the spell rank. On success that spell has no effect on you, though it resolves normally against other targets, and you gain temporary HP equal to spell rank + M. On failure it resolves normally and the use is spent.

source.originalText: Spell Absorption: Absorb a hostile spell, gaining temporary hit points equal to the spell's level.

completeCard.name: Minor Conjuration
completeCard.frequency: At will while RP remains; one object at a time
completeCard.effect: Minor Conjuration. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, conjuration. Create one nonmagical unattended object that fits inside a 1-foot cube, weighs no more than 10 pounds and is made of common nonvaluable material such as wood, cloth, clay, iron or glass. It cannot be food, poison, currency, a spell component with listed cost, ammunition with special properties or a functional complex mechanism. Creating another dismisses the first.

source.originalText: Minor Conjuration: Create a temporary, small inanimate object that lasts for 1 hour.

completeCard.name: Knowledge Transfer
completeCard.effect: Knowledge Transfer. Tags: hero, spellbinder, knowledge. Choose one language you can speak or one skill in which you are proficient. The ally gains proficiency in that language or skill for 1 hour. Expertise is never transferred. The feature conveys functional knowledge, not memories, secrets, class features, spellcasting or tool ownership.

source.originalText: Knowledge Transfer: Temporarily grant an ally knowledge of a skill or language you possess.

completeCard.name: Analyze Magic
completeCard.rangeAndTarget: One magical creature, object or effect within 30 feet
completeCard.effect: Analyze Magic. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, divination, knowledge. Make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + the effect's spell rank, treating a non-spell effect's Director-assigned tier as rank. On success learn its school or magical category, one active mechanical property and whether it is currently sustained, cursed or bound to another effect. Failure reveals only that magic is present.

source.originalText: Analyze Magic: Study a magical effect or item to gain insight into its properties and function.

automaticCards.name: Arcane Tradition
automaticCards.frequency: Automatic at Wizard 3; not a selection
automaticCards.effect: Arcane Tradition. Tags: arch, school, automatic. Your level-1 Arcane School becomes your Arcanist tradition; do not choose a second school. Prepare one additional matrix from that same school each day without counting it against your normal prepared-matrix maximum. It otherwise obeys all ordinary rank, spellbook, Dissonance and duplicate-family rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Tradition: Choose a school of magic to specialize in, gaining bonuses to spells of that school.

automaticCards.name: Counterspell
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One creature you perceive casting a spell within 60 feet
automaticCards.effect: Counterspell. Tags: arch-source, automatic, wizard-spell, abjuration, disruption. Trigger when a creature begins casting a spell. Make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + twice the spell's rank, treating rank 0 as 0. Success negates the triggering spell after its costs are paid; failure lets it resolve. This is gained automatically at Wizard 2 and is never also selected from the Arch pool.

source.originalText: Counterspell: Disrupt an enemy's spellcasting, potentially negating their spell entirely.

automaticCards.name: Elemental Affinity
automaticCards.duration: Permanent until changed by Core Sync
automaticCards.frequency: Automatic when Elementalist is chosen; counts as one level-10 Hero acquisition
automaticCards.effect: Elemental Affinity. Tags: hero, elementalist, elemental, automatic. Choose Fire, Cold, Lightning or Earth when entering Elementalist. Fire corresponds to fire damage, Cold to cold, Lightning to lightning and Earth to magical bludgeoning damage created by earth effects. Wizard spells matching the affinity gain +2 to their Wizard save DC or +2 on their spell attack, as applicable, and once per spell add one extra die matching that spell's primary damage die to one damage roll.

source.originalText: Elemental Affinity: Choose 1 element (Fire, Ice, Lightning, Earth); all spells of that element gain +2 DC, +1 damage tier

automaticCards.name: Ritual Casting
automaticCards.cost: 0 RP unless the individual ritual explicitly states otherwise
automaticCards.frequency: At will outside encounters with sufficient time
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5184. Cast a Wizard spell bearing the Ritual tag directly from your spellbook without preparing it. Increase its casting time by at least 10 minutes. Ritual Casting cannot be completed during an encounter, does not use an ordinary prepared-matrix position and does not generate or vent normal casting Dissonance.

source.originalText: | 2 | Counterspell Reaction, Ritual Casting |

automaticCards.name: School Mastery
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5186. This is the one School Mastery progression grant, not a second school choice or duplicate feat. Increase the level-1 Arcane School spell-attack and spell-save bonus from +1 to +2 total. Its school passive and bonus-spell rules otherwise remain unchanged.

source.originalText: | 5 | Bonus Feat: School Mastery |

automaticCards.name: Arcane Ward
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5187. After preparing spells, choose one of acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, psychic, radiant or thunder that is dealt by at least one prepared spell of your Arcane School. Gain resistance to that damage type until your next long rest. If none of your prepared school spells deals a damage type, choose force. This is provisional completion of the source's ambiguous 'chosen school's element' wording.

source.originalText: | 6 | Arcane Ward (resistance to chosen school's element) |

automaticCards.name: Dual Cast
automaticCards.cost: Pay the complete RP costs of both spells
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5188. Choose two DIFFERENT prepared Wizard spells of rank 1 or 2, neither of which summons a creature or grants an additional Action. Cast both sequentially as one Action, paying both RP costs. They cannot both require concentration. Each matrix separately updates first-cast/Refrain history. Features that trigger merely from 'casting a spell' may trigger once for each actual matrix unless that feature itself says once per turn; no trigger may create another Dual Cast or additional full Action.

source.originalText: | 9 | Dual Cast (cast 2 Tier 1–2 spells in a round) |

automaticCards.name: Overchannel
automaticCards.cost: Pay the Core V 2 RP cost for one rank above the spell's normal cast rank
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One prepared spell you are beginning to cast
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5190. Cast one prepared spell as though it were one rank higher than the highest rank at which you could normally cast that SAME spell, provided the spell has an explicit higher-rank scaling rule. Overchannel does not teach or prepare a higher-rank spell, cannot exceed effective rank 9 and cannot be combined with another generic Overcast rule during this pilot. All normal Dissonance/Refrain rules still apply.

source.originalText: | 13 | Overchannel (cast a spell 1 tier higher once/day) |

automaticCards.name: Arcane Feedback
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5191, converted from historical slot wording to RP. After your Counterspell successfully negates a spell, restore 1 RP, never above your normal maximum. A counter produced by a companion, reflected spell or copied Counterspell does not trigger this feature.

source.originalText: | 15 | Arcane Feedback (after successfully countering a spell, recover 1 RP once per round) |

automaticCards.name: Tethered Cast
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One concentration Wizard spell you cast this turn that targets only yourself or one willing ally
automaticCards.frequency: At most once per round; only one Tethered Cast active at a time
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5192. After casting the qualifying spell, tether it. The tethered spell no longer occupies your one normal concentration slot for up to 3 rounds. When damage would require a concentration save for the tethered spell, make the save normally; failure ends only the tether. Starting another Tethered Cast ends the existing tether first. A Tethered Cast cannot itself tether Spell Tether's second spell or permit more than two simultaneously sustained Wizard effects.

source.originalText: | 17 | Tethered Cast (bonus action spell link 1/round) |

schoolAutomatic.effect: ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.
